definition: In artificial intelligence, a differentiable neural computer (DNC) is a memory augmented neural network architecture (MANN), which is typically (but not by definition) recurrent in its implementation.
details: The model was published in 2016 by Alex Graves et al. of DeepMind.

explainer.lead: A differentiable neural computer is a neural network design that adds memory to the network, giving it somewhere to retain information while it works. It belongs to the family of memory-augmented neural networks and is often implemented as a recurrent system.

tiers.eli5: It is like a student who can jot notes in a notebook and look them up later, instead of having to keep everything in their head.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers implement it as a controller network coupled to an addressable memory matrix with differentiable read and write heads, trained end-to-end. A pitfall is that memory addressing is complex and training is delicate and costly compared with simpler architectures.
tiers.paperLevel: A differentiable neural computer is a memory-augmented neural network architecture, typically though not necessarily recurrent, published by DeepMind in 2016. Limits: it is research architecture with demanding training and addressing complexity rather than a standard production component.

components.name: Neural network
components.detail: The learned processing part of the architecture, commonly implemented recurrently.

components.name: Augmenting memory
components.detail: The memory that distinguishes the DNC from a neural network without this augmentation.

flow: The neural network performs the learned computation.
The architecture augments that computation with memory.
In a typical recurrent implementation, processing continues across successive steps.
explainer.origin: The model was published in 2016 by Alex Graves et al. of DeepMind.
explainer.whyItMatters: It makes memory augmentation an explicit part of neural-network architecture, while leaving room for both recurrent and non-recurrent implementations.

diagram.caption: A DNC combines neural-network processing with augmenting memory; recurrence is typical but not definitional.

explainer.example: A DNC is trained on a task requiring recall of earlier inputs, learning to write them into memory and read them back when needed.
